extractedWith: tools/extract/extract.ps1 -Batch p6-fe-att-widget -Manifest <scratch copy of allowlist.manifest.yaml with the p6-fe-att-widget batch> -Staging <scratch folder outside the repo> -Clean (scrub findings are expected before the rewrite; secret scan clean)
promotion: Each staged file was read as a reference only and rewritten with starter names and structure; "target" is the repo file it informed, "stagedTarget" the path in the staging folder. Content is a rewrite, so the repo file hash differs from stagedSha256. Carried patterns only: one row per picked file with its own id (never the file name), files uploaded one at a time, teardown of running uploads when the view goes away, one download at a time, and a visible failure instead of a silent dead button. Left behind: the legacy base64 attachments, the dual-source (legacy + service) DTO and its id pairing, the source product's per-purpose blocks, role-specific loaders, business-rule limits and descriptions.

origins.note: Rewritten on ng-dga dga-file-upload (one control per attachment type) and dga-page-feedback; the third-party UI kit markup and the per-purpose blocks were not carried.

Pattern kept: one download at a time and a visible failure (now page feedback with errors.<CODE> and the reference code). The dual-source rows, the legacy base64 save and the role-specific loader input were left behind; downloads go through the shared adapter for any record.
Rewritten: per-file rows with status, progress and error now come from dga-file-upload; the native file input, the per-file description fields and the separate record step were not carried.

Patterns kept: per-file upload state on a row with its own id, sequential uploads, cancelling running uploads when the view changes. The client business limits, the description rule, the batch record call and its retry-with-stored-metadata were left behind: limits are per attachment type on the server, and each file is linked by its receipt as soon as it is stored.
